words.gloss: not looking behind (not considering the consequences)

literal: Standing in front, even if speaking without kindness, do not speak, standing in front, the word that does not look behind.
translation: Even if you speak ruthlessly to someone's face, do not speak words in their absence that you cannot stand by when you face them later.
modern: ஒருவருடைய நேருக்கு நேர் நின்று இரக்கமில்லாமல் பேசினாலும் பேசலாம்; ஆனால் அவர் இல்லாதபோது, பின்னர் அவரே நேரில் வந்து நிற்கும் போது எதிர்கொள்ள முடியாத சொற்களைப் புறங்கூறிப் பேசக்கூடாது.
explanation: This couplet contrasts direct, harsh criticism with backbiting. The poet states that it is acceptable to stand directly in front of someone and speak words completely devoid of kindness. However, one must never speak words behind their back that they cannot stand by or face up to when they meet them in person later. The key contrast is between the courage of direct, albeit harsh, confrontation and the cowardice of backbiting which cannot bear the light of a face-to-face meeting.
